title: Understanding Bias-Variance Decomposition
text: The bias-variance decomposition is a way to express the expected error of a model in terms of three components: the variance of the noise, the bias of the model, and the variance of the model.

title: Conditions for Bias-Variance Decomposition
text: The decomposition holds under certain conditions, such as when the loss function is squared error and the model is linear.

title: Loss Function Consideration
text: Consider whether the absolute loss function satisfies the conditions required for the bias-variance decomposition.

title: Analyzing Linear Models with Absolute Loss
text: Does the bias-variance decomposition hold for linear models when using absolute loss?
